title: Yuridia Announces Las Cartas Sobre La Mesa Tour 2027 in the U.S.: Here Are the Dates
summary: Following her historic shows in Mexico, the singer will bring her tour to 18 U.S. cities starting in February.
contentText:
Yuridia , dubbed the queen of regional Mexican music, is bringing her Las Cartas Sobre La Mesa Tour to the United States in early 2027, Billboard can exclusively announce on Tuesday (Sept. 8).

Promoted by Live Nation, the 18-date tour will begin on Feb. 4 at the Paramount Theatre in Seattle and wrap up on March 28 at The Theater at MGM National Harbor in Washington, D.C. Along the way, the singer will also perform in cities like Las Vegas, Houston, Dallas, Chicago and New York.

“What I enjoy most about touring in the U.S. is traveling by bus. I really love spending time with the musicians and dancers. I also bring my family, my kids, and I’m very happy discovering different cities,” Yuridia tells Billboard Español . “The shows are always different, there are always surprises, and it’s so much fun. I’m very excited to experience that again.”

The announcement comes after the Sonora-born artist made history as the first Mexican to sell out two consecutive dates at Estadio GNP Seguros in Mexico City on Sept. 3 and 4.

Yuridia’s Las Cartas Sobre La Mesa Tour follows her Sin Llorar Tour, during which she visited more than 80 cities across Mexico, Central America, the U.S. and Canada between 2024 and 2025. Ticket presales begin today (Sept. 8) at 12 p.m. local time, while general sales kick off on Sept. 11 at 10 a.m. local time via LiveNation.com .

Recognized as one of the most prominent female voices in Mexican regional music, the 39-year-old singer — born in Hermosillo, Sonora, and raised in Arizona — rose to fame in 2005 by participating in the second season of Mexico’s reality show La Academia before debuting as a solo artist with her album La Voz de un Ángel .

Throughout her career, she has released 10 studio albums, achieved multiple diamond, platinum and gold certifications, and sold over three million records in Mexico and Latin America. On the Billboard charts, she has placed hits like “Qué Agonía” with Ángela Aguilar, which entered the top 10 of Latin Airplay , as well as “Mi Eterno Amor Secreto” with Edén Muñoz and “Un Bendito Día” with Alejandro Fernández, both of which reached No. 1 on Regional Mexican Airplay .

Her latest single, “Que Se Vaya,” released on Aug. 20, offers a first glimpse of her upcoming studio album and will be included in her setlist for Las Cartas Sobre La Mesa Tour 2027.
